newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds fall but underlying strength seen.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds fall but underlying strength seen.

text.p: Argentine bonds fell Thursday but the decline of local issues was cushioned by a feeling of underlying strength.
Argentine Brady bonds, however, took the cue from a slump in U.S. treasuries, showing their higher sensitivity to U.S. markets.
"The local market resisted the decline in the U.S., the 'Pre 2' is firm as a rock," said a trader at a foreign bank.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.10 to 119.20. The dollar-denominated Bocon Provisional due 2007 declined $0.05 to 104.30
Traders said the local market's relatively small decline in the face of the large drop in U.S. treasuries was testimony to its underlying strength.

"I would recommend that investors take advantage of this correction to buy long duration bonds, especially peso-denominated ones," said Roberto Costa Bourdieu, senior fixed income analyst at Banco Rio de la Plata.
Market players said the market was quiet this session, in anticipation of the release of the U.S. September producer price index and retail sales report on Friday.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 6.45 percent from 6.36 percent.
